system_overview: This specification models the Paxos Commit algorithm, which achieves fault-tolerant distributed transaction commit by running a separate Paxos consensus instance for each resource manager's prepare-or-abort decision. It replaces the single coordinator of two-phase commit with a set of acceptors and a leader, tolerating F failures among 2F+1 acceptors. The classic two-phase commit protocol is obtained as the special case with a single acceptor (F=0). Only safety properties are specified.
actors_and_components: The system consists of three types of participants: (1) Resource managers that prepare or abort, and act on the global commit/abort decision. (2) Acceptors that participate in multiple Paxos consensus instances (one per RM) by processing phase 1 and phase 2 messages. (3) Leaders that coordinate ballot rounds by sending phase 1a and phase 2a messages and deciding the transaction outcome when sufficient votes are collected. Leader selection is not modeled; any process may act as leader.
state_variables: The system tracks three pieces of state: (1) A mapping from each resource manager to its current state (working, prepared, committed, or aborted). (2) For each RM-acceptor pair, the acceptor's state in that RM's consensus instance, consisting of the highest ballot number the acceptor has responded to, the ballot number and value of its most recent vote (or sentinel values if it has not voted). (3) The set of all messages ever sent, which grows monotonically. Message types include: phase 1a (ballot initiation from leader), phase 1b (acceptor response with vote history), phase 2a (leader proposal with value), phase 2b (acceptor vote), and commit/abort announcements.
initial_state: All resource managers are in the working state. Every acceptor's state for every RM instance has its highest-responded ballot set to the initial ballot, no previous vote recorded, and no value voted for. No messages have been sent.
actions: Resource manager actions: (1) Prepare: a working RM transitions to prepared and sends a phase 2a message for ballot zero with value prepared. (2) Choose to abort: a working RM transitions to aborted and sends a phase 2a message for ballot zero with value aborted. (3) Receive commit: an RM seeing a commit announcement transitions to committed. (4) Receive abort: an RM seeing an abort announcement transitions to aborted. Leader actions: (5) Phase 1a: a leader initiates a new ballot for a specific RM instance by sending a phase 1a message. (6) Phase 2a: when the leader has received phase 1b messages from a majority of acceptors for a given ballot in a given RM instance, it determines a safe value and sends a phase 2a message. If all responding acceptors reported no previous vote, the leader chooses aborted; otherwise it uses the value from the highest-numbered previous vote. (7) Decide: when all RM instances have a value chosen by a majority (all prepared means commit; any aborted means abort), the leader announces the result. Acceptor actions: (8) Phase 1b: an acceptor responds to a phase 1a message if the ballot number exceeds its current highest ballot, updating that ballot and reporting its vote history. (9) Phase 2b: an acceptor votes for the value in a phase 2a message if the ballot number is at least its current highest ballot, updating its ballot and vote records.
safety_properties: Type correctness: all state variables remain within their declared types. The specification implements the abstract transaction commit specification, ensuring consistency: no resource manager is committed while another is aborted.
model_bounds: Constants include the set of resource managers, the set of acceptors, the set of majorities (each being a subset of acceptors such that any two majorities overlap), and the set of ballot numbers (which must include zero and be a subset of natural numbers). For model checking, typical values are two resource managers, three acceptors, three majority sets of size two, and ballot numbers zero and one.
additional_assumptions: Messages are modeled as a set that only grows; no message loss or duplication is modeled explicitly since only safety is specified. The initial ballot (ballot zero) is used by RMs to directly propose their prepared/aborted decisions, bypassing phase 1 for that ballot. A helper function computes the maximum of a set of numbers, returning negative one for the empty set. The specification imports the abstract transaction commit module and asserts that Paxos Commit implements it via refinement. Any two declared majorities must have a non-empty intersection.
